the title, called by the script at $0806 once the TP file is loaded. Shows the first picture (its screen copied from $1800-$1BFF, its colours from $1C00-$1FFF, the bitmap at $2000 in video bank 0, white border and background) for a delay of 12 x 65,536 turns of the loop at $805E, then the title scene ($80D3, $8260, $8374): starts the tune ($9000 with A = 0), sets the raster interrupts ($827E) and loops until space or fire on joystick 2, or until both the credits ($83C9) and the tune ($9016) have ended. Space or fire first fades the tune out ($9006 = 5) and waits 120 frames ($80CE); then the raster interrupt is switched off, the screen blanked and it returns.

starts tune A: A times 8 indexes the tune's entries ($FE); the tune's transpose ($96A6) goes into the add at $925A; the SID is cleared ($9305), the volume set to 15 (the operand at $90D2), the voices' state cleared, each voice released ($901B = $FE) at the start of its order list, and the tune turned on ($9016 = 1).

one frame of the tune, while $9016 is set: the volume (the operand at $90D2) to $D418, each voice's shadow registers to the SID; a fade-out step every $9006 frames, the tune stopping at volume 0; then at the end of each tick, for each voice, the release of the gate at its release point and the next pattern byte when the note's time runs out ($9171); and every frame each voice's effects ($931B).
the SID's volume, the operand of the lda at $90D1: 15 at the start, counted down by the fade-out.
silences the three voices (frequency 0) and turns the tune off ($9016 = 0).

reads the voice's pattern ($F2,x through $96A7/$96D7, position $F5,x). At the pattern's end ($FF) it plays it again while $9024 counts down, then reads the voice's order list (through $969F, position $F8,x): $FF and a position loops it, $FE ends the tune, $80-$FF sets the transpose, $70-$7F the instrument offset, $60-$6F the repeats, and anything below is the next pattern. In the pattern, $FC and a byte sets the fade-out ($9006), $E0-$FF is a rest of that length, $C0-$DF an instrument, $80-$9F the note length, $60-$7F an arpeggio, and below $60 a note: the note plus the voice's and the tune's transposes. A new note takes its instrument's waveform, envelope, pulse and effects ($97DE), unless it is tied ($FB after it).
the operand of the adc # that adds the tune's transpose to each note, written by the init ($9091); the code from here stores the note and starts it with its instrument.
sets the test bit and clears the gate of each voice, then zeroes the SID's registers $D400-$D41F.

one frame of a voice's effects. On a new note: a drum start ($9895: a first waveform for a few frames) and the vibrato's set-up ($97E3, $97E4). Then the vibrato, after its delay, sweeping the frequency up and down by a step derived from the next semitone; the pitch drop in the last five ticks of a note (bit 5 of $9031); the pulse program; the waveform and note programs (bit 7); the end of the drum start; and the arpeggio (bit 6).

the operand of the sbc # of the end-of-note pitch drop, written at $942A and $9436 (half the step on every other frame); the code from here sets the frequency's high byte lower and goes on to the pulse program.
the operand of the cmp # with the pulse sweep's top limit for the pulse width's high byte, written at $9474 from the program's second byte; the code from here turns the upward sweep at the limit.

the operand of the cmp # with the pulse sweep's bottom limit for the pulse width's high byte, written at $946E from the program's first byte; the code from here turns the downward sweep at the limit and goes on to the waveform program.
the operand of the ldy # that picks the note program, written at $9503 with the waveform program's number; the code from here reads the voice's note program.

the operand of the lda # that holds the note program's step, written at $954B; the code from here adds it to the note (bit 7 clear) or takes it as a note of its own (bit 7 set) and sets the frequency.
